newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Rains hit Czech flood areas, rivers seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Rains hit Czech flood areas, rivers seen rising.

text.p: Rain fell overnight across the flood-swept Czech Republic and storms expected at the weekend could trigger a new wave of the flooding that has devastated parts of the south and east, forecasters said on Friday.
At least 46 people have been killed in the worst killing on Czech territory for a century, and a similar number have died in Poland.

Light rain had been falling since the middle of the night in the east of the country and storms were expected to bring an average 30 millimetres (1.2 inches) of rain over the weekend, the Czech Weather Service said.
Thousands of homes and other buildings have been destroyed in two weeks of floods caused by days of torrential rain.
"If the rainfall is intense, which is very realistic, there might be more flooding but I am not able to estimate the extent," forecaster Michal Veverka of the Czceh Hydrological Centre told Reuters.
Water levels in the affected areas were falling on Friday but were expected to rise with the fresh rain. The ground is so saturated that any rain will rapidly raise the level of rivers, Veverka said.
River authorities have been emptying dams on the Vltava, which runs through the capital Prague, and on other rivers to make way for the expected downpour.
